policy: MajorMUD 1.11p gameplay parity excludes Worldgroup/host account-session, mail, weather/day-night, native administrative interface, host security handoff, native logging/diagnostics, and crash/startup behavior. Mixed requirements retain only player-visible MajorMUD gameplay semantics. Generic environmental-hazard abstractions are also excluded as Reforged extensions; native room effects remain owned by actual decoded MajorMUD room/exit mechanisms.

evidence.claim: MajorMUD is installed and entered as a module under Worldgroup; Worldgroup server setup/security exists outside the MajorMUD game module.
Worldgroup security keys and the WCCMMUD.INI SYS_*_KEY settings form a host-to-module authorization handoff rather than multiple intrinsic MajorMUD administrator levels.
Official MajorMUD help documents MajorMUD-owned game commands, parties, gangs, communication, saving-on-exit and other in-realm behavior separately from the surrounding BBS login/menu layer.
Operator-confirmed project scope excludes Worldgroup mail, host login/session/line limits, native logging/diagnostics, weather/day-night, native SYSOP interface parity, and crash/restart behavior.
Reforged administration is intentionally exposed through the editor while MajorMUD gameplay-visible effects remain subject to parity.
Stock RoomType 0-24 has no generic environmental-hazard record family; room damage/status effects remain represented by actual trap/cast/text/remote-action/etc. mechanics.
evidence.source: Pass 25 room schema closure / Nightmare Redux RoomType parameter map

evidence.reason: Generic RuntimeWorldContainerService is not a standalone Classic MajorMUD subsystem. Native death piles, banks/vault currency, gang-house vaults, portable item ownership, and treasure-chest loot remain with their actual gameplay owners.

Generic RuntimeTrapService charges/rearm/reset model is a Reforged extension shell, not the Classic type-09/type-24 parity owner. Classic exit traps remain owned by RuntimeClassicExitTrapCatalog and native RoomRec state.
